events.title: BoE MPC decision — hold at 3.75% expected
events.why_it_matters: Sixth consecutive hold is ~75-80% priced, but August CPI at 3.1% on war-driven fuel and a possible hawkish 6-3 split (Pill/Greene/Mann) keep a surprise hike live a day after the Warsh Fed.
events.what_to_watch: Vote split, QT envelope, and whether the statement treats energy inflation as a one-off or a second-round risk.

events.title: US August housing starts and building permits
events.why_it_matters: July starts already collapsed 12.4% to 1.239M SAAR; consensus is only a partial rebound to ~1.30-1.31M starts and ~1.40-1.41M permits as mortgage rates sit near a 5% 10-year.
events.what_to_watch: Single-family starts vs permits; a second down-leg would confirm the post-Lennar freeze in new construction.

events.title: SEMICON India 2026 (New Delhi)
events.why_it_matters: Modi opened a 600-exhibitor, 50-country chip gathering (ASML, Applied, Micron, Tata) as AI demand stays hot and governments push diversification away from single-node risk.
events.what_to_watch: Capex/JV announcements and any incentive packages that pull equipment orders from US/JP/NL toolmakers.

events.title: Electra Therapeutics IPO (ETRA)
events.why_it_matters: Largest biotech IPO in the window (~$325-347M at $14-16) tests clinical-stage risk appetite after Holtec pulled its nuclear listing into a hawkish-rate tape.
events.what_to_watch: Final price vs range and first-day trading; a stumble would freeze other healthcare listings.

events.title: BoJ decision — 25bp hike to 1.25% widely expected
events.why_it_matters: A 31-year-high policy rate landing a day after a hawkish Fed is the classic yen-carry unwind trigger, especially with oil imports already blowing out the trade deficit.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda presser on terminal rate, JGB buying, and whether guidance implies 1.50% by March 2027.

events.title: Bessent–He Lifeng talks on targeted tariff cuts
events.why_it_matters: Treasury confirmed a weekend meeting to tee up reciprocal cuts on ~$30bn of energy, ag, and manufacturing inputs plus a possible one-year extension of the Busan trade truce.
events.what_to_watch: Any joint readout on soy/energy purchases, rare-earths, and whether the $30bn package is locked before Xi lands.

events.title: PBOC September LPR fix — hold expected
events.why_it_matters: 1y/5y LPRs sit at 3.00%/3.50% while FAI is collapsing; a hold would confirm Beijing is not rushing a big easing even as consumption wilts.
events.what_to_watch: Any surprise 5y cut (mortgage benchmark) vs another hold that leaves property and credit demand in a rut.

events.title: AutoZone Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Best high-frequency read on US consumer trade-down and DIY auto spend into a rate-hike/oil-shock tape; Street is ~$54.42 EPS / $6.71bn sales.
events.what_to_watch: Same-store sales, DIY vs DIFM mix, and gross-margin commentary on parts inflation.

events.title: UNGA 81 high-level debate; Trump speech
events.why_it_matters: Trump speaks the morning of Sept 22 (after Brazil) overlapping the Xi visit and Iran/IAEA track; remarks on Hormuz, China, and Ukraine can move oil, defense, and tariff-sensitive names.
events.what_to_watch: Language on tanker-war de-escalation, Ukraine talks, and any UN-stage tariff/China framing ahead of Sept 24.

events.title: Trump–Xi Washington summit
events.why_it_matters: Highest-stakes trade event of the quarter: tariffs, rare earths, AI, Taiwan arms, and the Iran war, with the Nov 2026 Busan truce expiry looming and US midterms six weeks out.
events.what_to_watch: Truce extension length, any $30bn reciprocal cuts, and whether Taiwan/export-control language leaks into the communique.

events.title: Costco Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Membership-club bellwether for middle-income spending power as gasoline, rates, and food inflation squeeze real incomes; consensus ~$6.55 EPS / ~$94.9bn sales.
events.what_to_watch: Traffic vs ticket, membership-fee commentary, and any guidance cut tied to fuel/food inflation.

events.title: Darden Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Casual-dining bellwether (Olive Garden et al.) for lower/middle-income dine-out as energy and rates bite; Street ~$2.05 EPS / ~$3.21bn sales.
events.what_to_watch: Same-restaurant sales, traffic mix, and commodity/labor cost guidance.

events.title: US August new home sales
events.why_it_matters: Follows Lennar's order/margin miss and a 2026-low existing-home print; another drop would show builders cannot offset rate shock with incentives.
events.what_to_watch: SAAR vs inventory months-supply and median price; a sub-consensus print would hit homebuilders and lumber.

events.title: US Section 338 import bans on selected Canadian goods
events.why_it_matters: Sept 8 proclamations escalate the Canada tit-for-tat from 50% tariffs (modified Sept 15) to outright bans on specified beer/wine/spirits, some dairy, and motorcycles effective Sept 29.
events.what_to_watch: CBP enforcement lists, Canadian counter-retaliation, and any auto-tariff spillover beyond the current product set.

events.title: JOLTS August job openings
events.why_it_matters: Labor-demand read the day before PCE/GDP; a still-tight openings print would validate the Warsh Fed's 'resilient activity, elevated inflation' hike path.
events.what_to_watch: Openings, quits rate, and any cooling that markets could use to fade additional 2026 hikes.

events.title: August PCE + Q2 GDP third estimate
events.why_it_matters: Fed's preferred inflation gauge is nowcast ~3.7% headline / ~3.3% core YoY after energy shock; GDP third estimate is expected unrevised at +1.5% — stagflation-adjacent vs hawkish dots.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE m/m (0.24-0.32% range) vs SEP inflation upgrade; a hot core would reprice a second 2026 hike.

events.title: Micron FY Q4 earnings (HBM/AI memory)
events.why_it_matters: Sector bellwether for the AI memory supercycle: company guided ~$50bn revenue / ~$31 EPS with HBM sold out through 2027; print lands same day as PCE.
events.what_to_watch: Q1 FY27 guide, HBM4 ramp, and any sign pricing/capacity is peaking.

events.title: Nike Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Global brand-demand and Greater China read-through into a tariff/oil/rate squeeze; consensus ~$0.44-0.45 EPS / ~$11.4bn sales.
events.what_to_watch: North America vs China growth, inventory, and full-price vs promo mix.

events.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: First hard activity pulse after the Warsh hike and into oil-shock input costs; prices-paid vs new-orders split will tell if stagflation is hitting the factory floor.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs 50, new orders, and prices-paid; a sub-50 print with hot prices is the ugly mix.

events.title: FOMC 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% and hawkish SEP
events.why_it_matters: Unanimous first Warsh hike; 16 of 18 dots want at least one more 25bp move by year-end and inflation forecasts were lifted (headline PCE ~3.7%).
events.what_to_watch: Whether markets fully price a second 2026 hike before Sept 30 PCE, and 10-year/mortgage pass-through.

events.title: August advance retail sales rebound +1.2% MoM
events.why_it_matters: Sales jumped to $773.9bn (+1.2% MoM, +6.0% YoY; control group +1.4%), stronger than the prior scan's +0.6% print, softening recession fears even as gasoline inflated the headline.
events.what_to_watch: Whether real (ex-price) control-group strength holds into Costco/AutoZone and September PCE outlays.

events.title: Japan August trade deficit widens on oil imports
events.why_it_matters: Deficit hit ~¥1.11tn (fourth straight shortfall) as crude import values jumped ~59% YoY even while chip and auto exports stayed strong — the BoJ's inflation/hike backdrop.
events.what_to_watch: Yen reaction to Friday's hike and whether energy-import bills keep widening in September.

events.title: Lennar Q3 miss — orders and margins compress
events.why_it_matters: Deliveries -3%, orders -9%, ASP $372k, home-sale GM 15.8% (from 17.5%); double-miss and trimmed FY deliveries are the housing-bellwether confirmation of rate shock.
events.what_to_watch: Today's starts/permits and Sept 24 new-home sales for confirmation that the freeze is broadening.

events.title: Holtec Nuclear IPO (HNUC) suspended
events.why_it_matters: One of the window's largest energy IPOs (~$750-900M) was pulled on market conditions the day of the Fed hike, a risk-off signal for AI-power/nuclear listings.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Electra still prices and if other energy IPOs slip past October.

events.title: Google ad-tech remedies: no breakup, 6-year conduct rules
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected DOJ's AdX divestiture, imposing interoperability, data-sharing, anti-self-preferencing, and a monitor — another behavioral-not-structural Big Tech outcome.
events.what_to_watch: DOJ/Google appeals and whether advertisers actually multi-home away from AdX.

events.title: ECB 25bp hike; deposit rate to 2.50%
events.why_it_matters: Second 2026 hike, unanimous, driven by Middle East energy shock; staff see inflation 3.0%/2.5%/2.1% in 2026-28 and Lagarde refused to pre-commit — next meeting Oct 28-29.
events.what_to_watch: Whether euro-area energy pass-through forces another hike in late October.

events.title: US August CPI 0.4% MoM / 3.4% YoY; PPI +5.4% YoY
events.why_it_matters: Energy-heavy CPI and still-hot PPI were the data that locked in the Warsh hike and lifted SEP inflation dots; core CPI 0.3%/2.4% was less extreme than headline.
events.what_to_watch: Sept 30 PCE conversion of these prints; next CPI is Oct 14 (outside window).

events.title: August existing-home sales 3.98M SAAR
events.why_it_matters: Sales -2.0% MoM to a 2026 low with 4.9 months' supply (highest since 2015) as inventory finally rebuilds into unaffordable mortgage rates.
events.what_to_watch: Today's starts and Sept 24 new-home sales for whether the freeze is spreading from resale to new build.

events.title: China August activity: IP +5.2%, retail +0.4%, FAI -7.2%
events.why_it_matters: Export/high-tech factories are fine (robots, batteries, 3D printing) while domestic demand and investment wilt — a deflationary China demand shock into a global oil shock.
events.what_to_watch: Whether weekend Bessent–He talks and the LPR hold leave Beijing still refusing a large stimulus.

events.title: OPEC+ 7 keep October quotas unchanged
events.why_it_matters: Core producers held October targets after completing the 188kbd September unwind; actual barrels remain below quota because of Iran-war disruptions, so the 'hold' does not add supply where it is missing.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 4 mini-meeting and whether Hormuz losses force a formal compensation/boost discussion.

events.title: US–Iran tanker war / Hormuz disruption
events.why_it_matters: Tit-for-tat tanker strikes (US hits on IRGC-linked carriers Sept 5 and 8; Iran claiming ~10 ship attacks) keep Strait traffic far below pre-war norms and Brent around $104-105.
events.what_to_watch: Daily transit counts, diesel cracks, and any UNGA/Xi-summit de-escalation language; next OPEC+ review is Oct 4.

events.title: Ukraine peace-talks shuttle; October trilateral eyed
events.why_it_matters: Witkoff/Kushner met Putin (Sept 5) and Zelenskyy (Sept 6); Kyiv says it is preparing for October talks, but territory remains the blocker and fighting continues.
events.what_to_watch: UNGA sideline meetings and any energy-infrastructure truce; a real ceasefire would ease European gas/defense premia.

events.title: BoK tightening pressure after Fed hike; Korea AI-chip boom
events.why_it_matters: Back-to-back July/August hikes to 3.00% already delivered; Aug minutes showed a rift and the Fed hike adds pressure for another move as HBM/AI capex overheats growth and inflation (~3.1%).
events.what_to_watch: November BoK meeting odds and any power-grid/KEPCO bottleneck news around Samsung/SK mega-fabs.

events.title: FY2027 CR already signed through Dec 11 — shutdown risk quiet
events.why_it_matters: House 370-48 / Senate 90-6 CR (P.L. 119-103) funds government through Dec 11, so the Sept 30 fiscal-year turn is not a shutdown event this cycle.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing in this window; next fight is post-midterm December.

events.title: August NFP +162k; unemployment 4.1%
events.why_it_matters: Labor still 'keeping pace' in the Fed's own words — not weak enough to block a hike, not hot enough to scream overheating — and the next jobs print is Oct 2 (outside window).
events.what_to_watch: Sept 29 JOLTS as the only labor update before PCE.

top_risks: Hormuz tanker war keeps Brent ~$104-105 and diesel elevated, feeding another Warsh hike and a stagflation tape
Hawkish SEP (16/18 dots want ≥1 more 2026 hike) plus a BoJ move to 1.25% triggers a yen-carry / global duration unwind
Trump–Xi summit fails to extend the Busan truce or delivers Taiwan/export-control friction instead of $30bn tariff cuts
Housing freeze (Lennar miss, 3.98M existing sales, 5% 10-year) broadens into starts/new-home sales and regional-bank credit
China demand collapse (retail +0.4%, FAI -7.2%) meets oil shock — global growth down, inflation up
top_opportunities: Weekend Bessent–He talks and Sept 24 Trump–Xi deliver targeted tariff cuts plus a one-year truce extension
AI/HBM supercycle (Micron Sept 30, Korea mega-fabs, SEMICON India) remains the one clear earnings/capex offset
US consumer still spending (retail +1.2%, control +1.4%) if oil merely stabilizes rather than re-spikes
Google ad-tech ruling avoids breakup, reducing a left-tail for mega-cap communication services
Shutdown risk is off the table until December, removing a late-September fiscal cliff
summary: The Warsh Fed has hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% with a hawkish SEP, while BoE (today, hold expected) and BoJ (Friday, 1.25% hike expected) complete a synchronized G3 tightening into $104-105 oil. The two-way overlay is still Sept 24 Trump–Xi and weekend Bessent–He talks on ~$30bn tariff cuts versus an unresolved Hormuz tanker war; housing is already cracking (Lennar, existing sales) even as nominal retail sales rebounded +1.2%.
